title: 6 Powerful, Soul-Searching Things To Say To Difficult Students difficult-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Following reader questions about a prior article on talking to difficult students, Linsin offers six specific phrases meant to be delivered without requiring a response, each tied to a particular moment: 'You're better than that' after misbehavior, 'This is not who you are' at the end of a bad day, 'That's not good enough' after modest improvement, 'You can do this' before a challenging task, 'Now that is how you do it!' after real, sustained success, and 'I believe in you' after a student hits rock bottom. He explains the reasoning behind each phrase and stresses these words only carry weight when accountability is already in place and when spoken with genuine, honest conviction rather than as manipulation.
points: The article catalogs six short, purposeful phrases for difficult students, each matched to a specific behavioral moment.
These statements are designed to be left with students to 'ponder, marinate in, and grapple with' rather than to prompt an immediate response.
Words only carry meaning when students are already being held accountable for their behavior through a working classroom management plan.
'That's not good enough' is framed counterintuitively as a morale booster rather than a criticism, signaling belief in a student's higher potential.
Because difficult students can detect insincerity, the phrases only work when delivered with genuine conviction rather than as manipulation.
quotes: It is both a statement of fact and a challenge. And coming from someone they respect, four little words never said so much.
Through their words and actions, most teachers communicate to difficult students that their misbehavior is who they are, all but guaranteeing that poor behavior will not only continue, but get worse.
Difficult students are used to receiving heavy praise for modest improvement, and so this statement can come as a shock.
Because they’ve known so many of them, because they’ve been manipulated, coddled, indulged, and falsely praised ten times over, difficult students can pick a phony a mile away.
So when you appear unexpected, like a guardian angel from on high, and deliver the message they most need to hear… It will echo in their head long after you’ve turned and walked away.
